'''Rami Grossberg''' ({{Langx|he|רמי גרוסברג}}) is a full professor of [[mathematics]] at [[Carnegie Mellon University]]. He works in [[model theory]].

==Mathematical Work==
Grossberg's work revolves around the development of a model-theory for classes that cannot be axiomatized by [[First-order logic|first-order]] sentences. His early work includes:

* (with Shelah) Finding that under the [[weak continuum hypothesis]] there is no universal object in the class of uncountable locally finite groups<ref>{{Citation | last1=Grossberg | first1=Rami |last2=Shelah | first2=Saharon| title=On universal locally finite groups | journal= Israel Journal of Mathematics | pages=289-302 | volume=54 | year=1983 | doi=10.1007/BF02761988}}</ref>.
* Generalizing the Keisler–Shelah omitting types theorem for <math>\mathit{L(Q)}</math> (first-order logic with the quantifier "there exists uncountably many") to successors of singular cardinals<ref>{{Citation | last1=Grossberg | first1=Rami | title=Models with second order properties in successors of singulars | journal= The Journal of Symbolic Logic | pages=122-137 | volume=54 | number=1 | year=1989 | doi=10.2307/2275020}}</ref>.
* (with Hart) proving a structure theorem for <math>\mathit{L}_{\omega_1,\omega}</math> (first-order logic, but with countably infinite conjunctions and disjunctions), which resolves [[Spectrum of a theory|Morley's spectrum problem]] for the so-called "excellent" classes<ref>{{Citation | last1=Grossberg | first1=Rami | last2=Hart | first2=Bradd | title=The Classification of Excellent Classes | journal= The Journal of Symbolic Logic | pages=1359-1381 | volume=54 | number=4 | year=1989 | doi=10.2307/2274819}} </ref>.
* (with Shelah), showing that there is a jump in cardinality of the [[Ext functor|abelian group]] <math>\text{Ext}_p(G, \mathbf{Z})</math> at the first singular strong limit cardinal<ref>{{Citation | last1=Grossberg | first1=Rami |last2=Shelah | first2=Saharon | title = On the structure of Extp(G, Z)|
journal = Journal of Algebra|
volume = 121|
number = 1|
pages = 117-128|
year = 1989|
doi = 10.1016/0021-8693(89)90088-4}}</ref>.

Grossberg later work focuses on [[Abstract Elementary Class|Abstract elementary classes]], a framework for model theory of non first-order classes that encompasses many infinitary logics as a special case (including the aforementioned <math>\mathit{L}_{\omega_1,\omega}</math> and <math>\mathit{L}(Q)</math>). While the definition of the framework is due to Shelah, Grossberg wrote the first expository paper on the topic. The paper gives the definition of these classes, proves many key facts, and lists open problems<ref>{{citation
 | last = Grossberg | first = Rami
 | contribution = Classification theory for abstract elementary classes
 | contribution-url = https://www.math.cmu.edu/~rami/Rami-NBilgi.pdf
 | doi = 10.1090/conm/302/05080
 | mr = 1928390
 | pages = 165–204
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society | location = Providence, RI
 | series = Contemporary Mathematics
 | title = Logic and algebra
 | volume = 302
 | year = 2002| isbn = 978-0-8218-2984-4
 }}</ref>. As of 2026, it has become Grossberg's most cited paper<ref>{{Google Scholar id|q1g_W5sAAAAJ}}</ref>.

In joint work with [[Monica VanDieren]], he gives a proof of an "upward" [[Morley's categoricity theorem|Morley's Categoricity Theorem]] for [[abstract elementary class|Abstract Elementary Classes]] with the amalgamation property, that are [[Tame abstract elementary class|tame]]<ref>{{Citation| first1 = Rami | last1=Grossberg | first2=Monica | last2=VanDieren | title = Categoricity from one successor cardinal in tame abstract elementary classes |
journal = Journal of Mathematical Logic| 
volume = 06| 
number = 02|
pages = 181-201|
year = 2006|
doi = 10.1142/S0219061306000554}}</ref>. 

The tameness property used in the paper has turned into an independent notion of interest. It has led for example to new understanding of the notion of [[Forking extension|forking]] in the abstract elementary class setting <ref>{{Citation| first1 = Boney | last1=Will | title = Tameness and extending frames |
journal = Journal of Mathematical Logic| 
volume = 14| 
number = 02|
page = 1450007|
year = 2014|
doi = 10.1142/S021906131450007X|arxiv = 1308.6006}}</ref>. The research program on tameness remains active <ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Boney | first1 = Will | last2 = Vasey | first2 = Sebastien
 | contribution = A survey on tame abstract elementary classes
  | pages = 353–427
 | publisher = CRC Press
 | editor = José Iovino
 | title = Beyond First Order Model Theory
 | year = 2017
 | arxiv = 1512.00060
 }}</ref>. A joint work with Sebastien Vasey proves for examples that numerous candidate definitions of [[superstable theory|superstability]] are all equivalent in the tame context. This gives evidence that sizable fragments of [[stable theory|classification theory]] generalize well to the abstract elementary class framework<ref>{{citation | last1=Grossberg|first1=Rami|last2=Vasey|first2=Sebastien|title=Equivalent definitions of superstability in tame abstract elementary classes|volume=82|doi=10.1017/jsl.2017.21| number=4| journal=The Journal of Symbolic Logic|year=2017|pages=1387-1408|arxiv=1507.04223}}
</ref>.

Grossberg's students have written more than 60 papers under his guidance, mostly on abstract elementary classes <ref>{{Cite web |title=Rami Grossberg - Student papers |url=https://www.math.cmu.edu/~rami/Student_papers.html |access-date=2026-02-09 }}</ref>.
